gaps.sentence: ___ of her two brothers lives abroad.
gaps.explanation: 'Each of her two brothers lives ...' is correct; 'every' cannot take 'of' and 'both/all' need a plural verb.

gaps.sentence: We inspected the four bridges, but ___ of them was safe.
gaps.explanation: 'None of them was ...' is used for three or more items; 'neither' is only for two.

gaps.sentence: I asked ___ in the office, but nobody knew the answer.
gaps.explanation: 'I asked everybody' (all the people) contrasts with 'nobody knew'; 'everything' refers to things, not people.

gaps.sentence: There is so ___ crime in this area that people are afraid.
gaps.explanation: 'So much' is used with uncountable nouns like crime; 'plenty' would need 'of'.

gaps.sentence: ___ time I visit Rome, I discover something new.
gaps.explanation: 'Every time I ...' introduces repeated occasions; 'all time' and 'whole time' are not used here.

gaps.sentence: There isn't ___ room for another desk in here.
We can take the ferry or the tunnel — ___ way takes about three hours.
gaps.hint: one of two options, singular noun
gaps.explanation: 'Either way' means whichever of the two you choose; 'both' would need 'ways'.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the two films has been shown on television.
gaps.explanation: 'Neither of the two films has ...' is correct for two items; 'none' is not used for two and 'both/all' need a plural verb.
